summary: The oldest international scholarship programme in the world brings students from around the world to the University of Oxford for postgraduate study. It pays Oxford's fees and a living stipend, plus visa and travel costs, for up to three years.
covers: University of Oxford course fees, and the Oxford application fee.
A stipend of £20,400 a year (£1,700 a month) at the 2025–26 rate.
Student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge fees, and two economy flights — one to the UK at the start and one home at the end.
A settling-in allowance on arrival. Funding runs for the length of your course, up to three years for a DPhil.
eligibility: Scholarships are awarded by constituency — groups of one or more countries — and a Global Rhodes Scholarship covers applicants from countries without their own constituency.
Each constituency sets its own age limit, degree requirements and deadline, so read your constituency's page first.
Selection looks for academic excellence, character, leadership and commitment to others.
how_to_apply: Find your constituency on the Rhodes House website and read its eligibility rules and deadline.
Choose an Oxford postgraduate course and apply through the Rhodes online system with a personal statement, academic statement, CV, transcripts and references.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by the constituency's selection committee, usually in the autumn.
Rhodes Scholars then apply to Oxford for their chosen course; the scholarship starts in October of the following year.
watch_out: Applications for the 2027 Rhodes Scholarship (starting October 2027) were open when we checked — most constituencies close between June and early October.
Deadlines and age limits differ by constituency. Missing yours means waiting a year.
Your personal statement must show who you are, not just what you have achieved — generic essays stand out for the wrong reasons.
